claim: Test an AI-scaling thesis by linking compute, power, capital expenditure, supply constraints and adoption timelines to price-implied expectations.
The price of the whole company, which is the only thing a price-implied timeline can be solved against. Same construction and same output id as the other seats that build it.

The part of the price that the cash the business already produces pays for. The remainder is what the market has bought on a future it cannot yet see delivered, and that remainder is the closest thing to a price-implied timeline these facts will yield.
Reject conclusions whose load-bearing input is private or classified.
Reject a scale scenario that lacks a dated, financeable power path.
Reject a timeline that ignores documented equipment and interconnect lead times.
Excluded claim: a claim to reproduce the named researcher's current view
Known limit: Important laboratory capabilities and state planning inputs may be private or classified.
Known limit: The public thesis is recent, so resolved long-horizon decision cases are inherently scarce.
